title: The quotation と, compound verbs and nouns
summary: と closes whatever came before it into a single quoted unit. Verbs and nouns can also be glued together to make new words.

blocks.text: Two words for "thing". **もの** is a concrete object (a hat, a book, a mountain). **こと** is an abstract matter or circumstance: something that happens or is the case.

This と is a different particle from the "and" と. It works like a spoken quotation mark. It follows speech or thought, usually with **言う** (say) or **思う** (think). Whatever comes before it, a single word or an entire clause with its own grammar, is wrapped up into one unit that modifies the verb after it.

blocks.jp: 猫は「面白いことがない」と言った。
blocks.en: The cat said, "Nothing interesting is happening."

blocks.jp: 兄は「遅い！」と言って、走り出した。
blocks.en: My brother said "I'm late!" and burst into a run.

blocks.text: The same idea carries to sounds and manner: ぴょんぴょんと is a hopping "quote" that describes how someone moves.

blocks.jp: うさぎはぴょんぴょんと走り続けた。
blocks.en: The rabbit kept running, hopping along.

blocks.text: Stick the **い-stem** of one verb onto another verb and you get a new meaning. 出す adds "suddenly begin", 続ける adds "keep doing", 過ぎる adds "pass", and 込む adds "into, with force".

Two nouns can simply be placed side by side, with no の. The first sound of the second noun often turns voiced (a **か** becomes **が**, a **そ** becomes **ぞ**, a **と** becomes **ど**). This is called 連濁. As a rough rule it happens often with native (kun) readings: 青 + 空 = 青空 (あおぞら), 懐中 + 時計 = 懐中時計 (かいちゅうどけい).
Finally, a て-form plus **ください** is a polite request, and ください can be dropped: ちょっと待って(ください).

blocks.jp: ちょっと待ってください。

items: **もの** = concrete thing; **こと** = abstract matter.
**…と言う / 思う**: と wraps what comes before it into a quote.
Compound verb: **い-stem + another verb** (走り出す, 飛び込む).
Compound noun: two nouns side by side, the second often voiced (**青空**).
